text:
Hi AlexC,

Thank you for commenting on my homework, btw our name is the same.:) I'm sorry if the picture is confusing but the arrow is meant to show the direction of the compression not pointing at the spike up. The way I see it, is as it compressed down, it took all the supply above (the unfilled orange box is an absorbed supply) so when it reached the blue box (demand), there's no supply above and price can easily went up to the orange box (supply).

Correct me if I'm wrong, thanks again:)

author: justinasjot
text: Hello Ladies and Gents, I made my homework about compression. As far as I understand compression is all about price cleaning it’s way up to supply (or down to demand). I made 5 examples. In each one minor demands are marked as D1/D2/D3 and ect. Hope it will not confuse you. In those charts I tried to show where demand was taken out and where some buy orders where left – and how does the price reacted to pending orders left. Any comments would be really appreciated. If there are mistakes left – please show them to me – everybody is learning from mistakes.
